scenes.title: What is a Diode-Connected MOSFET?
scenes.narration: A diode-connected MOSFET is a transistor with its gate and drain shorted together. This simple configuration forces the device to act like a two-terminal resistor.

scenes.title: Small-Signal Impedance
scenes.narration: Because the gate and drain are tied, the small-signal impedance looking into the device is approximately one divided by its transconductance, or one over gm.

visual.formula_where: Z is impedance, gm is transconductance, and gmb represents the body effect.

scenes.title: Key Trade-offs
scenes.narration: In amplifier circuits, these act as loads. Higher gain requires a weaker load, but using these devices consumes voltage headroom, limiting your total output voltage swing.
